subject: Agriculture
title: Fair Trade and Farming
description: A micro-lesson that makes Fair Trade and Farming usable.

hook.text: A coffee farmer in Ethiopia earns 2% of what you pay for a latte. Fair Trade tries to fix that.

buildup.text: Fair Trade guarantees a minimum price to farmers, plus a premium for community investment—schools, clinics.

discovery.text: Certified Fair Trade products have grown into a $10 billion market across coffee, chocolate, and bananas.

twist.text: Critics argue the premium rarely reaches the poorest workers—it flows to cooperative leaders and certified farms.

climax.text: Fair Trade raises awareness of farmer poverty but can't solve structural power imbalances in global supply chains.

punchline.text: Buying Fair Trade helps. Changing trade rules would help more.

quiz.question: What does Fair Trade certification guarantee to farmers?
options: A minimum price plus a premium for community investment

details.summary: Fair trade certification guarantees minimum prices and social premiums for farmers in developing countries. This topic covers how fair trade works, its impact on coffee, cocoa, and banana producers, and the debate about whether it truly helps the poorest farmers.
details.whyItMatters: Fair trade addresses the power imbalance between small farmers and global buyers. Over 1.7 million farmers participate in fair trade, and it has become a model for ethical consumer activism.
takeaways: Fair trade guarantees minimum prices and social premiums for certified producers
Coffee, cocoa, bananas, and tea are the largest fair trade commodity categories
Critics argue fair trade benefits mainly mid-sized cooperatives rather than the poorest

faq.question: How does fair trade certification work for farmers?
faq.answer: Farmers organize into cooperatives that meet social and environmental standards. Buyers pay a guaranteed minimum price plus a social premium. The premium funds community projects like schools, wells, and clinics chosen democratically by the cooperative.

faq.question: Does fair trade really help the poorest farmers?
faq.answer: Research shows mixed results. Fair trade improves income stability and funds community projects, but the poorest farmers often cannot afford cooperative membership fees or meet certification requirements. Benefits tend to concentrate among better-organized mid-sized producers.
